transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-07 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Ortiz (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nia Roberts (Redwood CSM); Laura Singh (Helios Procurement), Derek Moss (Helios Security), Priya Raman (Helios ML), Tom Alvarez (Helios Legal), Chris Yuen (Helios Platform)

Summary:
- Purpose: align procurement/legal on MSA/DPA exceptions, validate security/KMS pathing, and agree pilot acceptance criteria and pricing band for a 6-week technical pilot.
- Outcome: agreed action items; procurement indicated conditional approval pending SOC2 and clarified egress fees; security wants a pilot-bound hardened config and escrow for logs for 30 days.

Topics covered:
- MSA/DPA redlines, privileged key handling (KMS/HSM), data residency and egress costs, SLA thresholds for latency, pilot scope and success criteria, timeline to PO and technical pilot kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving out time. i'm Maya, account executive on the redwood side, with evan and samir on the engineering side. quick roll call?
[00:18] Laura Singh: hi yep, laura here from procurement. we've got legal and sec on the line, tom and derek. priya and chris representing ML and platform.
[00:30] Tom Alvarez: tom from legal — just here to listen and flag anything on the MSA / DPA side.
[00:36] Derek Moss: derek, security architect. big concerns for us are KMS integration, audit logs, and network egress.
[00:44] Maya Chen: perfect. objective for today is to confirm the gate list so procurement can move to conditional approval, and to get alignment on what the pilot needs to prove technically.
[00:55] Evan Ortiz: i can walk through the pilot topology and the hardened config we usually recommend for pilots — VPC peering, private subnets, and tenant-level keying.
[01:06] Priya Raman: quick Q, what's the default data retention for logs during a pilot? we may need a shorter retain window for PII.
[01:14] Nia Roberts: from CSM side we typically set pilot log retention to 30 days, and we can provide redacted logs; we can also toggle PII redaction filters.
[01:24] [small cross talk] Chris Yuen: when you say tenant-level keying — do you mean customer-managed keys?
[01:29] Evan Ortiz: yes, CMK support is supported — we integrate with major KMS providers; there's option for bring-your-own-key or Redwood-managed with HSM-backed key wrapping. sometimes the transcription shows K V cash but sorry, that's KMS K M S —
[01:44] Laura Singh: ok, procurement needs to see the network diagram and who has access to logs. can you share SOC2 and the network diagram for the dedicated topology?
[01:53] Maya Chen: 100%. We'll share SOC2 report and a sanitized network diagram. i'll add that to the action items.
[02:05] Tom Alvarez: on the DPA — we have a few redlines around subprocessor disclosure and data deletion certification. are you able to provide an attestation for deletion after pilot?
[02:18] Samir Patel: yes we can provide post-pilot deletion certs for datasets we touch in the pilot. there are two modes: hosted api with default retention policy, or dedicated pool that gives you isolation and configurable retention.
[02:33] Derek Moss: if we do dedicated, is the traffic egress billed differently? procurement is worried about variable egress costs.
[02:41] Maya Chen: good callout — there are three pieces: compute token billing, storage, and egress. procurement often asks for an egress cap for pilots; we can offer a fixed egress allowance for the 6-week pilot and then reconcile.
[02:57] Laura Singh: that would make approval easier. can you put the egress cap proposal in writing?
[03:03] Maya Chen: yes, we'll propose a pilot egress cap and the reconciliation mechanism.
[03:10] [00:03:10] Priya Raman: on success criteria — for us latency and hallucination rate matter. specifically we want 95th percentile latency under 250ms for a 512-token seq and hallucination under 2% on our eval set.
[03:26] Evan Ortiz: understood, we can run baseline microbenchmarks. historically those numbers map to a mid-tier quantized variant; we'll include model recommendation + quant profiles in the pilot runbook.
[03:38] Priya Raman: also we need to validate KV cache behavior under bursty traffic — sometimes the KV cache is mis-typed in notes as K V cash —
[03:46] Samir Patel: yeah — KV cache, continuous batching and prefix caching — we'll include a workload test in the runbook with synthetic bursts to validate tail latency.
[03:55] Derek Moss: regarding keys — we need timing on key rotation, and can we get attestation that keys are never exported from HSM?
[04:03] Evan Ortiz: rotation is supported via customer-managed keys; key material is HSM-wrapped and we can provide an architectural diagram and KMS policy templates showing keys aren't exportable.
[04:14] Tom Alvarez: legal will want the specific DPA clause edits; we're asking for a more explicit subprocessor list and 30-day deletion attestation. also we need to confirm data residency in region us-west-2 for the pilot.
[04:29] Maya Chen: region pinning for pilot is ok — we can provision in us-west-2. on the subprocessor list, we provide a current list and a commitment to notify for changes. we'll flag the 30-day deletion attestation as an addendum to the DPA for the pilot.
[04:45] [short pause, someone typing]
[04:50] Laura Singh: procurement also asked about invoicing cadence — pilot is usually billed monthly? we want a PO for pilot cost to be processed before start.
[04:59] Maya Chen: standard practice is a monthly invoice, but for pilots we can accept a single PO for the pilot term up front; we'll include the pricing band for the fixed egress allowance.
[05:10] Chris Yuen: operational question: how do we handle LDAP / SSO onboarding and RBAC for the pilot?
[05:16] Samir Patel: SSO via SAML is available, we can federate with your identity provider. RBAC controls can be scoped to reviewer / operator / admin roles. for the pilot we typically set two platform admins and a few observer roles.
[05:29] Priya Raman: is there an option for private deployment (on-prem) if vendor evaluation goes well?
[05:35] Maya Chen: yes — we have Redwood Private options, but that's typically a separate commercial track. pilot is meant to validate functionality; if you want a migration path to private later we can map that out.
[05:47] Derek Moss: any encryption-at-rest certs? which FIPS or NIST standards do you meet?
[05:52] Evan Ortiz: we can provide a compliance summary — FIPS 140-2 level for HSMs used by our KMS partners, TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit, and AES-256 at rest. i'll add a note to send our compliance doc.
[06:08] Tom Alvarez: another legal note: indemnity and liability caps — we need to line these up with our vendor policy. can redwood accept a contractual clause that limits exposure in certain ways?
[06:18] Maya Chen: we can take those redlines through our legal team — for enterprise deals there's room to negotiate liability caps and we can flag which are standard exceptions and which need executive approval.
[06:29] [06:29] Laura Singh: timeline question — procurement wants pilot kickoff by 2026-08-24. is that realistic?
[06:36] Maya Chen: if we get conditional approval and PO by 2026-08-17, yes we can aim for kickoff 2026-08-24. it depends on the SOC2 and network diagram turnaround.
[06:48] Nia Roberts: CSM will run an onboarding checklist; typical lead time for a pilot is 5 business days after PO and credentials are provisioned.
[06:58] Priya Raman: for the evaluation dataset, will we send data or run locally? we prefer a hybrid where we upload sanitized test sets to the tenant and keep PII masked.
[07:08] Samir Patel: hybrid works — we can provide guidance for data sanitization and a sample ingestion script.
[07:15] Derek Moss: can you commit to audit log retention for the pilot? we need at least 30 days and a way to export logs for our SIEM.
[07:23] Evan Ortiz: yes export is possible via S3 push or syslog; we'll document the export hook in the runbook.
[07:30] Tom Alvarez: network egress — can you confirm egress is charged from the region where data leaves, and if there are cross-region transfers?
[07:39] Maya Chen: egress is billed by datacenter region; we'll explicitly call out cross-region egress and offer the pilot cap to limit surprises.
[07:49] Laura Singh: regarding pricing — our procurement needs at least two pricing bands: pilot band and estimated production band. can you provide both?
[07:57] Maya Chen: yes — we'll provide a pilot quote and an indicative production tier with commitment discounts.
[08:06] [brief silence]
[08:12] Priya Raman: one more technical ask — can we run a translation/embedding test? our stack relies on embeddings for reranking and we want to see embed latency and cost.
[08:22] Samir Patel: embeddings are supported; we'll include cost-per-embedding numbers and sample scripts for batch processing and streaming API.
[08:31] Derek Moss: do you have data residency controls if we later require EU-only processing?
[08:36] Maya Chen: yes, we can pin to regions; for EU residency that's part of the onboarding for production and we'd discuss in a separate track.
[08:45] Tom Alvarez: back to the DPA — subprocessor notifications, deletion attestation, and the 30-day log retention addendum are the main asks from legal.
[08:53] Maya Chen: got it. we'll prepare a DPA addendum for the pilot that includes deletion attestation, subprocessor list snapshot, and log retention addendum.
[09:02] Laura Singh: any blockers from redwood's side on signing a pilot PO?
[09:06] Maya Chen: none — commercial is happy to accept a pilot PO with the capped egress and the pilot pricing band.
[09:13] [09:13] Priya Raman: for the model suggestion, can you recommend quantization profiles for latency vs cost tradeoffs?
[09:20] Evan Ortiz: yes, we'll include three profiles: low-latency high-cost (FP16), balanced (INT8-ish quant), and low-cost (8-bit quant with some quality tradeoffs). we'll give benchmark numbers for each.
[09:34] Chris Yuen: operational runbook question — if we hit an incident during pilot, what's the escalation path?
[09:40] Nia Roberts: support levels: CSM first line, then Sev-level oncall engineering. for pilots we provide a named SE and an escalation SLA for critical incidents.
[09:51] Derek Moss: do you provide audit logs that show key access events?
[09:55] Evan Ortiz: yes key access and key policy changes are logged; we'll show an example audit log format.
[10:02] Tom Alvarez: legal wants to see a redline of the MSA that highlights our requested exceptions. we'll provide those back to you by 2026-08-11.
[10:11] Maya Chen: great — we'll consolidate and route to legal.
[10:16] Laura Singh: can we summarize the immediate deliverables? procurement needs SOC2, network diagram, pilot quote with egress cap, and PO window.
[10:27] Maya Chen: summary — action items: 1) SOC2 + sanitized network diagram (redwood) 2) Pilot runbook + benchmark scripts (redwood SE) 3) DPA addendum with deletion attest + subprocessor snapshot (redwood legal) 4) Procurement to confirm PO timeline and pricing band (helio)
[10:46] [closing]
[10:50] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with an email that has the action items and target dates. we'll aim to share the documents by EOD Monday. any last questions?
[10:58] Laura Singh: no, thank you. appreciate the clarity.
[11:03] Tom Alvarez: thanks, bye.
[11:06] [call ends]

References and attachments mentioned:
- SOC2 report (to be shared, redacted)
- Sanitized network diagram (Redwood Dedicated topology)
- Pilot runbook (to be provided by SE)
- DPA addendum draft (to be produced by Redwood legal)

Notes on transcript fidelity: automated transcription had a few mis-keys ("K V cash" for KMS/K V cache) and speaker overlaps in parts of the discussion; legal jargon occasionally truncated.

End of transcript.
